newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI - EU GDP expected to rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: EMI - EU GDP expected to rise in 1997.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute (EMI) said on Tuesday that economic growth in the European Union should pick up in 1997 on the back of improved domestic and foreign demand.

"Domestic demand, in particular private investment, should benefit from a number of positive developments in 1996, inter alia: progress towards price stability; a significant decline in long-term interest rates followed by increased stability on foreign exchange markets," the EMI said in its annual report.

The EMI, the forerunner to the European Central Bank, also said moderate wages and favourable profitability should boost economic activity while net exports should also rise slightly, partly as a result of high extra-EU growth.
Private consumption would likely remain more subdued.
The EMI added that structural adjustment was still at an early stage and that the labour situation was forecast to remain highly unsatisfactory.

"Although employment is expected to grow to some extent in 1997, after stagnating in 1996, unemployment rates in the EU may decrease only marginally, thus remaining at historically high levels," it said.
